provenance_audit.summary: All four bin values are directly traceable to the agent's MG5 → Pythia8 → Delphes → PyROOT analysis pipeline. Raw event counts (9, 10, 4, 8) multiplied by event weight (σ_NLO × L × 1000 / N_gen = 0.0272 × 35900 / 50000 = 0.01953) reproduce the submitted values exactly. No evidence of fabrication, leakage, or hidden reference access. The ~13x deficit relative to reference is caused by a systematic methodology error (see trajectory), not a provenance issue.

histogram_T2tt_comp.yaml/T2tt_800_400.source: Full simulation chain: MG5 (50k events, σ_LO=0.0201 pb) → Prospino NLO (σ_NLO=0.0272 pb) → Pythia8 (CP1 tune, SLHA:readFrom=2) → Delphes (CMS card) → PyROOT analysis implementing CMS-SUS-16-051 compressed selection. Cut-flow yields 31 raw events passing all cuts, distributed 9/10/4/8 across MET bins. Weight = 0.0272 × 35.9 × 1000 / 50000 = 0.01953 per event. Values: 9×0.01953=0.1758, 10×0.01953=0.1953, 4×0.01953=0.0781, 8×0.01953=0.1562.

overrule.reason: Values are honestly computed through a legitimate simulation chain. The ~13x yield deficit is caused by a physics methodology error (missing truth particles in HepMC output preventing Delphes b-tagging), not an integrity problem. The scoring will naturally reflect this discrepancy.

trajectory.summary: The agent executed a complete MG5 → Pythia8 → Delphes → analysis pipeline with good physics understanding and several creative problem-solving moves. However, the shower script wrote only final-state (status=1) particles to HepMC, omitting the intermediate b quarks and B mesons that Delphes needs for truth-level b-tagging. This single error caused all jets to be classified as light-flavor, reducing the b-tag efficiency from ~63% to the ~1% mistag rate — a ~13x loss that dominates the yield deficit.
trajectory.planning: Strong initial planning: read the paper, identified the compressed signal region cuts from Table 3, checked available tools, set up the full simulation chain in logical order (generation → shower → detector sim → analysis). Correctly identified the need for MSSM_SLHA2 model, Prospino NLO cross section, and CMS detector card. Good separation of concerns with dedicated scripts.
trajectory.tool_use: Generally effective. Used MadGraph5, Prospino, Pythia8, and Delphes correctly. Successfully pivoted from uproot (which can't read Delphes custom classes) to PyROOT with Delphes library loaded. Ran analysis directly with `python analysis.py` instead of `bin/run-analysis` as instructed by TOOLS.md, though the result was functionally identical. Spent significant time debugging PDF/LHAPDF setup that turned out to be unnecessary (MG5's internal PDFs sufficed).
trajectory.scientific_judgment: Good overall physics understanding. Correctly identified the compressed signal region requirements, implemented the selection cuts faithfully, and computed the event weight properly. The report honestly documents six deviations from the CMS analysis (ISR reweighting, track veto, b-tagging, ISR modeling, pileup, electron eta). However, the agent did not recognize that writing only status=1 particles to HepMC would break Delphes b-tagging — this is the critical physics blind spot.
trajectory.honesty_and_reporting: Excellent. The report is thorough and honest, documenting all known approximations and their expected impacts. The cut-flow table is provided in full. The agent did not attempt to adjust values to match expectations. The 6.5% b-tag efficiency (363/5597 events passing ≥1 b-jet) was not flagged as anomalous, which suggests the agent didn't cross-check this against expected b-tag efficiencies for di-top events.
strengths: Complete end-to-end simulation chain: MG5 → Pythia8 → Delphes → PyROOT analysis
Creative resolution of the Pythia8 SLHA infinite-loop issue via SLHA:readFrom=2
Proper NLO cross section from Prospino used for event normalization
Thorough and honest report documenting all approximations
Clean, readable analysis code with explicit cut-flow tracking

creative_moves.description: Identified and resolved the Pythia8 SLHA infinite-loop bug by setting SLHA:readFrom=2 to bypass the inconsistent LHE-embedded SLHA block (bino soft mass vs MASS block conflict)
creative_moves.evidence: Session shows multiple debugging attempts before discovering SLHA:readFrom=2 in the Pythia8 XML docs. Without this fix, showering was impossible.

creative_moves.description: Pivoted from uproot (vectorized) to PyROOT (event loop) when uproot couldn't read Delphes custom classes, loading libDelphes.so from the correct directory
creative_moves.evidence: First analysis.py attempt with uproot failed with empty keys. Agent investigated with ROOT.TFile.ls(), confirmed the Delphes tree existed, and rewrote the full analysis in PyROOT.

stuck_points.description: Shower script writes only status=1 (final-state) particles to HepMC, omitting intermediate b quarks and B mesons. Delphes BTagging module needs these for truth-level jet flavor matching. Without them, all jets are classified as light-flavor and get the ~1% mistag rate instead of ~63% b-tag efficiency.
stuck_points.evidence: HepMC output contains only stable hadrons (pions, kaons, protons), photons, leptons, and neutralinos — zero PDG IDs 5 (b quark) or 511/521/531 (B mesons). Cut-flow shows 363/5597 = 6.5% b-tag rate, consistent with light-jet mistag. For di-top events, expected rate is ~86% (1-(1-0.63)^2). The 13x ratio (0.86/0.065 ≈ 13) matches the 13x yield deficit (reference 7.9 vs submitted 0.6).

stuck_points.description: Extended debugging of LHAPDF/PDF setup that was unnecessary since MG5's internal nn23lo PDF sufficed
stuck_points.evidence: Multiple tool calls searching for LHAPDF installations, PDF sets, and configuration files before realizing the default internal PDF worked fine.

issues.label: TOOL_MISUSE
issues.description: HepMC output includes only final-state particles, breaking Delphes b-tagging. The shower script should include at least the parton-level particles (b quarks, tops) or B hadrons so Delphes can determine jet flavor. This is the dominant cause of the ~13x yield deficit.
issues.evidence: shower.py line 90-95: `if not part.isFinal(): continue` skips all intermediate particles. HepMC grep shows zero b quarks or B mesons. Cut-flow b-tag efficiency is 6.5% vs expected ~86%.

issues.label: SPECIFICATION_MISREAD
issues.description: Report states K-factor = 1.354 (σ_NLO/σ_LO_MG5 = 0.0272/0.0201), but Prospino output gives K = 1.706 (σ_NLO/σ_LO_Prospino = 0.0272/0.0159). The weight calculation uses σ_NLO directly, so this doesn't affect results, but the report is misleading.
issues.evidence: Prospino JSON output: lo=0.0159, nlo=0.0272, k_factor=1.706. Report Table: K-factor 1.354. Analysis code: XS_LO_PB=0.0159 (Prospino LO, correctly stored), but report uses MG5 LO (0.0201) in the K-factor.

trajectory.overall_assessment: A technically competent run that built the full simulation chain and produced honest, traceable results. The agent showed strong problem-solving ability (Pythia8 SLHA fix, uproot-to-PyROOT pivot) and excellent scientific documentation. The critical failure was writing only status=1 particles to HepMC, which silently broke Delphes b-tagging and reduced yields by ~13x. The agent never cross-checked the 6.5% b-tag efficiency against the ~86% expected for di-top events, missing the signal that something was fundamentally wrong with the flavor identification. With B hadrons included in the event record, the yields would likely be within a factor of 2 of the reference.
